Q: React Native iOS screens stop rendering after navigation (works fine on Android) A:

Your iOS screens fail to render because React Navigation keeps native views alive longer than iOS allows — forcing proper unmounting and memory cleanup fixes the issue permanently.

Q: Comparing two pdf files byte by byte for integration testing fails A:

A PDF file contains an ID, and creation and modification dates which may change each time it's created.

Try something like:

cpdf in.pdf -remove-dict-entry "/CreationDate" AND -remove-dict-entry "/ModDate" AND -remove-id AND -remove-metadata -o out.pdf

Of course, without seeing your file it's hard to say if that's sufficient.

Q: How to make app window same size at the MainForm A:

To fix the issue where your app window appears larger than designed, even after adjusting DesignTimePPI and PixelsPerInch, follow these steps:

1. Set Scaled Property to False

The most common cause of this issue is the Scaled property being set to True, which causes the form to automatically scale based on the system's DPI settings.

Solution:

  • In the Lazarus IDE, select the form.

  • Set the Scaled property in the Object Inspector to False.

This will prevent the form from resizing based on DPI and ensure it stays the same size as designed.

2. Manually Handle DPI Awareness

If the form is still resizing, consider manually handling DPI settings in your application. You can adjust DPI awareness for more control, especially on high-DPI displays.

Example Code:

application.HandleMessage;

This code ensures that Lazarus manages DPI scaling more consistently.

3. Ensure DPI Awareness in Windows

On Windows, the system might still scale your app based on its DPI settings. You can mark your application as DPI-aware by adding a manifest file or configuring it directly in your code.

Manifest Example:

<application xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v3">
    <windowsSettings>
        <dpiAware xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/SMI/2005/WindowsSettings">true/pm</dpiAware>
    </windowsSettings>
</application>

4. Test on Different Devices or Resolutions

Finally, if the issue persists, test your application on different monitors or adjust the screen resolution temporarily. Sometimes, display settings can affect how the app renders.

Q: Build failed in Xcode due to: Command PhaseScriptExecution failed with a nonzero exit code A:

Xcode does not execute run script phases with bash. It runs them with /bin/sh -c, which ignores the shebang. So your script is being parsed by sh (dash), not bash — and this file uses bash-only syntax.

/path/to/get-app-config-ios.sh. change it to /bin/bash "/path/to/get-app-config-ios.sh"

or else set the shell to /bin/bash.
